#+TITLE: The CPAN distributions vendored into topology-perl
#+LANGUAGE: en
#+STARTUP: showall
#+OPTIONS: toc:nil num:nil

Sixteen distributions, installed in this order (=vendor/ORDER=) into
=/opt/topology/perl= by =bin/vendor-install.sh=, each tested first and each
checked against =vendor/cpan/SHA256SUMS=.  Versions, dates and authors were
read from metacpan on 2026-10-31; the sums are of the tarballs in
=vendor/cpan/=.

* The table

| distribution | version | released | maintainer (CPAN id) | tier | why it is here | sha256 (first 16) |
|--------------+---------+----------+----------------------+------+----------------+-------------------|
| Module-Build | 0.4234 | 2023-04-28 | LEONT (Leon Timmermans) | build | builds most of the above; left perl core in 5.22 | =66aeac6127418be5= |

Tiers: *core* is what =Topology= needs to load at all; *bridge* is what lets
the same code run on perl 5.36 to 5.40 (on 5.44 Feature::Compat::Class
needs nothing); *async* is =async=/=await=; *api* is =topology serve=;
*build* is what the others need to build.  The =ceiling= setting does not
remove packages; it only decides what runs.

* How they were chosen

The prompt asked for modules that "appear well maintained from contributors
that care of few things (but this well) or care for a larger number of
things and also contribute regularly to perl, itself."

OBSERVED (metacpan, 2026-10-31): eleven of the sixteen are by one author,
Paul Evans (PEVANS); eight of those were released in 2025 or 2026.  The
other five are toolchain pieces by Leon Timmermans (LEONT), Karen Etheridge
(ETHER), Graham Ollis (PLICEASE) and Jens Rehsack (REHSACK), last released
2019 to 2023: small, finished, and depended on by much of CPAN.

JUDGED (mine; check before relying on it): Paul Evans wrote perl's core
=class= feature (=perlclass= names him) and maintains Object::Pad, Future
and IO::Async, so the class syntax, its bridge and the async stack come from
the one person who has kept them in step: the "larger number of things, and
perl itself" kind.  Leon Timmermans and Karen Etheridge are long-standing
perl toolchain maintainers (the "perl itself" kind); Class::Inspector and
File::ShareDir are the "few things, done well" kind: unchanged for years
because they are done.  Falsifier: a dist here with open security reports
and no maintainer response, or a newer release that changes behaviour we
rely on; =bin/vendor-check.sh= is not written yet, so this is checked by
hand at each perl upgrade.

What we did not take, and why: Mojolicious (well maintained, but a whole
web framework where four routes are needed); Moo and Moose (object systems
the core =class= is meant to replace for new code); YAML::PP (TOPOLOGY.md
front matter is kept simpler than YAML on purpose, see the spec).

* Tests

On 2026-10-31 every one of the sixteen passed its own test suite under
perl 5.44.0 built for =/opt/topology/perl= (IO-Async: 1638 tests).  The
Topology modules pass under 5.44.0 (core class) and 5.38.2 (Object::Pad).
